rationale: Luke has the same exchange in the same order: the question about eternal life, the commandments, "Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me" (Luke 18:22, BSB), the man's sadness "because he was extremely wealthy" (18:23), the camel and "the eye of a needle" (18:25), "Who then can be saved?" (18:26), and Peter's "we have left all we had to follow You" (18:28). In this app's BSB the phrase "eye of a needle" occurs only in Matthew 19:24, Mark 10:25 and Luke 18:25. The type is parallel and the label strong, not explicit, following conn-matt16-confession-luke9: neither Gospel cites the other. Luke's differences can be checked. Only Luke calls the man "a certain ruler" (18:18); only Matthew calls him "the young man" (Matthew 19:20, 19:22); so the familiar title "rich young ruler" combines two Gospels. Luke's man says "Good Teacher" and hears "Why do you call Me good?" (18:18-19), as in Mark. Luke's list puts adultery before murder (18:20), the order of Swete's Septuagint at Deuteronomy 5:17-18; Matthew keeps murder first. Luke has no "love your neighbor as yourself" and no "If you want to be perfect." Luke's promise is "many times more in this age" (18:30), with no "hundredfold" and no twelve thrones; Luke has a saying about the Twelve on thrones at another point, at the Last Supper (22:28-30). Luke has no "first will be last" here (he has it at 13:30).
